decisions.decision: Combine the planned PFAS outreach mailing into a single postcard with a QR code rather than two separate mailers, and add QR code information to the town's ledger/website and the town manager's newsletter.
Confirmed the PFAS outreach/funding work is not urgent and can be split between this fiscal year and next depending on funding.
Agreed to brief the town manager or a select board member once the Keings final report is complete and asked that a select board liaison attend future meetings.
Agreed to repair the Autocar truck (roughly $10,000 in work) rather than replace it.
Agreed the superintendent and another commissioner will assess the Mac truck together and develop a realistic repair estimate rather than replace it immediately.
Indicated a preference for treating the Hickory Hills and Lancaster A wells together, rather than treating Keings alone, to address both PFAS and hardness.
Decided against pursuing a program to fund individual home water softeners, citing the district's responsibility to supply adequately treated water and unresolved maintenance/cost questions.
Agreed to follow up with the project engineers for more specific data on the dead-end line/stagnant water concern and the differing water qualities between well sites.

public_comment.topic: Praised the district's staff for their responsiveness during a major flood at his home.
Asked whether the redundant well planned at Keings was for added volume or to protect against a well casing failure.
Asked which of the engineers' six PFAS treatment options were actually viable for Lunenburg.
Asked about the cost of treating hardness and whether funding individual home water softeners could be a cheaper alternative.
Asked about well number three's bacteria contamination and how the wells interact with and affect one another.
Asked whether Lancaster water could be piped to Keings for combined treatment, raising the dead-end line/stagnant water concern.
Raised concerns about water supply, unknown maintenance/financial costs, and blamed 3M and DuPont for PFAS contamination, urging patience for federal or state action.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District Commissioners voted to hire Capital Strategic Solutions for PFAS-related public outreach and Mar Services for redundant well testing at Keings, and discussed repairing rather than replacing two aging trucks. Most of the meeting was extended public comment questioning PFAS treatment options, costs, and hard-water tradeoffs, in which commissioners said they would not fund individual home water softeners and leaned toward treating the Hickory Hills and Lancaster wells together rather than Keings alone, though no formal vote was taken on the treatment approach.

what_happened.line: Commissioners decided against a program to fund individual home water softeners for residents.
They leaned toward treating the Hickory Hills and Lancaster A wells together for PFAS and hardness, rather than treating Keings alone, though no formal vote was taken.
Commissioners voted to hire Capital Strategic Solutions for PFAS-related outreach and Mar Services for redundant well testing at Keings.
They agreed to repair, rather than replace, two aging district trucks.
The district switched its planned PFAS outreach mailing from two mailers to one postcard with a QR code to cut postage cost.

why_it_matters: Residents with hard water will not get district help paying for a home softener; any future treatment plant serving Hickory Hills and Lancaster could instead show up in water rates.
The direction chosen for well treatment is not yet a formal vote, so the cost and scope residents will eventually be asked to fund is still open.
PFAS outreach materials and mailings are how residents will get official information on well contamination and what, if anything, changes for their water.
